articles.headline: Auto mode is now the default in Claude Code for Pro, Max, and Team plans
articles.dek: Anthropic flipped the switch—auto mode comes pre‑enabled for all Claude Code users on Pro, Max, and Team tiers.

body.text: Key Takeaway

Starting today Claude Code runs with auto mode turned on out of the box for Pro, Max, and Team accounts, so you no longer need to add an `auto_mode` flag to your config [FACT:9d83146030362131e33b6a0455ff3709].
Why This Matters

Auto mode lets Claude decide when to invoke tool calls without explicit prompting, which trims prompt length and reduces the “enable auto mode” errors that have been popping up in CI pipelines [FACT:9d83146030362131e33b6a0455ff3709]. For builders, that means tighter iteration loops and fewer manual toggles.
What Happened

Anthropic announced the change in a short post on August 8, 2026, stating that the default setting for Claude Code on Pro, Max, and Team plans is now auto mode instead of manual [FACT:9d83146030362131e33b6a0455ff3709].
Builder View

If your scripts already set `auto_mode: true`, nothing changes; if you omitted the flag, Claude will now automatically decide tool usage, so your existing CI steps keep working without a code change [FACT:9d83146030362131e33b6a0455ff3709]. Teams that need deterministic behavior can still opt out by explicitly passing `auto_mode: false`.
Open Questions

Anthropic has not released latency or cost numbers for the new default, and it’s unclear whether legacy accounts will be auto‑updated or if per‑project overrides are planned [FACT:9d83146030362131e33b6a0455ff3709]. Builders should watch the pricing dashboard and run spot checks on edge cases where unintended tool calls could surface.
Ardur Take

The announcement comes from a single, verifiable source, so confidence in the fact that auto mode is now default is high, but operational impact should be validated in your own test harness before rolling out broadly [FACT:9d83146030362131e33b6a0455ff3709].
